blocks.sourceText: **Target:** a vanilla-JavaScript port of lokalized-java 3.0.0, pinned to CLDR 48.2.

- produces the same semantic result as lokalized-java for every shared behavioral vector when both
  implementations use the same pinned data and vector versions;

- treats the semantic result as the returned translation, lookup and resolved locales, attempted
  locales, status, failure reason, negotiation diagnostics, and specified thrown error behavior;

- works in Node, bundlers, and a plain browser `<script type="module">` without an application build
  step or runtime dependency;

- keeps loading asynchronous and explicit while keeping `createStrings`, `get`, `t`, and `getResult`
  synchronous;

- publishes language-neutral data and behavioral contracts that a Python or Go implementation can
  consume without reproducing JavaScript or JVM implementation details.
| Node | 22; CI also runs 24 and current | Installed-package tests against the packed tarball |
| Browsers | Safari 16.4, Chrome 111, Firefox 111 | Exact-floor smoke tests plus current Playwright engines |
| Modules | ESM only; CommonJS `require` is unsupported | Node ESM, bundler, and direct-browser tests |
| TypeScript consumers | `node16`/`nodenext` and `bundler` resolution | Generated declarations checked from a packed install |

The named browser floors are provisional until CI can exercise those actual releases. Playwright's
bundled current engines alone do not prove an old compatibility floor.

- interpolation, bidi isolation, expressions, all ten language-form axes, generated placeholders,
  exact decimals, ordinals, and cardinal ranges;
- explicit manifest planning and browser/Node loading;

- npm and direct-browser distribution, generated declarations, documentation, and a release-time
  parity declaration.
- date, time, number, percentage, currency, and list formatting; collation;

- React bindings, linting, a standalone conformance package, dashboards, and host-`Intl`
  optimizations; these are post-MVP proposals;
- TMS/XLIFF import, export, or round-tripping in v1;
- automatic I/O from `get`, hidden global caches, or mutable live-reload instances;
- runtime-limit customization in v1; Java-compatible defaults are fixed;
- strict parity claims for the optional host-`Intl` locale or plural implementations;

- the exact server negotiation solver in the root browser entry. Browser applications may consume
  an already-resolved locale or use the explicitly best-effort small browser chooser; the parity
  solver's additional range/header parsing and whole-list ranking code is an optional browser/edge/
  server subpath. Root already carries the pinned data and strict single-locale kernel used by direct
  diagnostics and the small chooser.

The API is specified below in TypeScript notation, but the implementation is vanilla JavaScript with

All returned records and arrays are defensively copied and frozen. `get`, `t`, `getResult`, and
`getDirectLocaleContext` are bound, referentially stable functions; `strings.t === strings.get`.

The export map and generated declarations are checked against a machine-readable symbol allowlist.
Root does not re-export loading, SSR, full negotiation, Node, or the ordinal/range subpaths' runtime
values and classifier functions, preventing those graphs from being pulled in accidentally. The
`OrdinalData` and `CardinalRangeData` carrier interfaces are type-only core/root exports; other
structural types may likewise be declaration-only re-exports without changing the runtime graph.

All non-Node paths are free of `process`, `Buffer`, filesystem APIs, and Node crypto. `lokalized/load`
requires Fetch, readable response bodies, `AbortController`, `TextDecoder`, and WebCrypto; other
non-Node paths require only the ECMAScript/browser floor stated in `1.1`. Deferred subpaths such as `lokalized/react`, `lokalized/locale-intl`, and
`lokalized/cardinality-intl` do not appear in the export map until implemented.
Direct-browser files retain `.js` names. npm public subpaths are extensionless.

The implementations remain peer repositories under a conventional sibling container:

~~~text
lokalized/
  lokalized-java/       reference implementation and interim data producer
  lokalized-js/         JavaScript consumer
  lokalized-cldr/       trigger-gated future shared generator
  lokalized.com/        documentation/site consumer
~~~

Implementations version independently. Compatibility is expressed by metadata, not matching package
versions:

A vector can provide:

- one or more raw strings-file fixtures with source names and locale tags;
- tiebreakers, fallback locale, callback fixture IDs, and registered data modules;
- a lookup key, locale or language ranges, typed placeholders, and per-call options;
- an expected result, failure-handler input, warning set, or thrown error/cause identity token.
Tagged decimal, plural-operand, and language-form records use the exact public wire shapes from `3.7`.
Callbacks are referenced by versioned fixture IDs rather than embedding executable code.

An ID names one semantic proposition, not one test method. IDs are never reassigned to unrelated
behavior. The corpus partitions cross-language `requiredPortableIds`,
`requiredImplementationIds` keyed by implementation family (for example JS browser/Node delivery),
and explicitly nonportable `informationalIds`. Every implementation reports exact applicable,
passed, failed, xfailed, and unsupported sets; counts are derived presentation only. Milestone
manifests report, but do not activate, the IDs whose registry activation milestone has been reached:
core through M7, JS delivery at M8, and negotiation at M9. Activation is derived under `8.6`.
An xfail requires severity, owner, reason, and expiry during development. A strict parity-backed

release requires every `requiredPortableId` to pass and empty failed, xfailed, and unsupported sets for
that partition. An implementation release must also pass every applicable
`requiredImplementationId`, but those cases do not inflate cross-language parity. Informational IDs may
be unsupported and never enter either numerator.

- The reference runner and generator execute in a repository-pinned Eclipse Temurin JDK 21 image. M0
  records the exact vendor, update/build string, and immutable image digest in
  `reference-runtime-lock.json`; the archive and parity report repeat them. This controls
  `Double.toString` and other host behavior without changing lokalized-java's `--release 9` consumer

contract. Values beyond JS safe integer range use tagged decimal/bigint/operand vectors, never an
  ambiguous bare JSON number.

Before plan approval starts M0, a checked bootstrap `requirements.json` contains every selected-
profile requirement whose `registrationBefore` frontier includes M0. During M0 it expands to the
complete initial registration slice, which also contains every selected-profile requirement whose
frontier includes M1, M3a, or M2. Before any post-M0 milestone in a requirement's frontier starts, its
applicable clauses are atomized, reviewed, and appended in a successor registry revision;
implementation or evidence from that milestone cannot count before the revision and successor
selection attestation are frozen. The complete semantic plan remains the M0 contract, but a later
clause does not acquire immutable requirement-record status until its registration batch.

Requirement IDs have the immutable form `LJ-<AREA>-NNN`; from first registration an ID is never
reassigned, and a retired requirement remains as a tombstone. Each registered non-retired record
contains exactly one atomic, independently verifiable proposition plus:
- the normative statement, its hash, and a stable source anchor;
- parity class: portable, implementation-required, or informational/nonportable;

- exactly one activation milestone, one owning exit milestone, and the release profiles to which it
  applies;

- a checked evidence expression, each evidence item's producer milestone, and the IDs of vectors,
  generated-corpus partitions, static checks, benchmarks, compatibility runs, or reviewed decision
  records that discharge it.

The statement hash is SHA-256 over the exact UTF-8 bytes of the statement value in the registry's JCS
projection, so whitespace or wording changes cannot drift silently. The reviewed bootstrap process
adds a clause-level marker with exactly one requirement ID to every M0-frontier proposition; M0 adds
the markers for the remaining M1/M3a/M2 initial-slice propositions. Multiple propositions are split
into separately marked clauses; an outer block may list its contained IDs for navigation but cannot
discharge them. Every remaining selected-profile normative block carries a
lightweight checked `DEFERRED-UNTIL:<milestone[,milestone...]>` marker naming its reduced registration
frontier. Before any named milestone starts, the block is atomized and its deferred marker is replaced
by registered IDs. M-R permits no deferred marker in selected-profile scope.

The linter knows the checked normative section/clause grammar. From first registration it checks every
registered record for a unique ID, a source marker, and a one-to-one exact statement hash; it also
rejects an unmarked clause inside the active closure or a deferred marker whose frontier has begun.
It does not infer semantic boundaries or atomicity. A reviewer attests atomicity when approving the
initial record, expansion, or migration. An explicit reviewed `NONNORMATIVE` marker is required for
rationale or examples inside the checked grammar.

Every behavioral and generated vector carries one or more `requirementIds`. Non-vector evidence uses
checked evidence manifests with the same IDs. Evidence references are conjunctive by default. An
explicit `anyOf` group is allowed only when the registry records a reviewed rationale that every branch
proves the same proposition; nested free-form Boolean expressions are forbidden. Each allowed evidence
kind has a schema-level machine acceptance predicate: vector, generated-partition, and compatibility
runs must execute the exact referenced ID set with every required result passing; static checks must
run the locked tool/command over the locked source/configuration, exit successfully, and satisfy their
declared zero-or-exact-finding predicate; benchmarks must meet the frozen threshold and tolerance under
their checked scenario; and decision records require separate reviewer approval plus immutable
input/result hashes. Acceptance is derived from those records, never asserted by a free status field.
A decision record cannot discharge a runtime-behavior requirement.

Every evidence attestation binds the exact canonical requirement-record hash and evidence-expression
hash it proves. It also carries a checked applicability projection: covered source-root tree hashes,
artifact or packed-tarball hash, data-lock hashes, and relevant configuration/tool hashes. Closure
recomputes that projection for the milestone subject; a mismatch invalidates the evidence and requires
a rerun. The only exception is an explicitly referenced reviewed non-impact static check whose locked
dependency analysis proves the changed subject is outside the evidence scope; prose or a decision
record alone cannot preserve runtime evidence. A statement/evidence-expression migration likewise
invalidates prior evidence unless the new expression explicitly references a reviewed equivalence
check, and all prior pass/fail/missing history remains immutable.

Before approval, the bootstrap process freezes `release-profiles.json` and one initial signed/approved
selection record. Each immutable
profile ID names its complete product/support claims and derives its applicable requirement set; the
selection record contains that ID plus the exact profile-registry and `requirements.json` hashes.
Every milestone-closure and release attestation repeats the selected profile ID and selection-record
hash, and closure requires the record's embedded hashes to equal the current registries. After every
registry expansion or reviewed requirements/profile-registry migration, a successor signed selection
attestation records the predecessor hash and current registry hashes; it may retain the same profile
ID. Changing the selected profile ID or claim set is specifically a reviewed claim-cut migration and creates a new
immutable profile/selection record. Every successor retains the prior selection, failures, and missing-
evidence history and cannot retroactively make an earlier gate pass.

Activation is derived mechanically from each registered requirement's activation milestone and
selected release profile; a milestone manifest cannot omit an applicable requirement or activate one
itself. In the dependency DAG, each
activation milestone and every declared evidence-producer milestone must be an ancestor of or equal to
the owning exit milestone. For a registered record, changing statement text, parity class,
activation/owner milestone, release profile, canonical evidence expression, reference IDs, producer
milestones, scenario/acceptance-policy identity, or retirement requires a reviewed
migration record containing old/new canonical records, reason, and approver identity. Section links
remain navigation aids, never identity. CI rejects duplicate, reused, unknown, source-unmarked, or
hash-mismatched registered IDs; an unmarked clause inside the active closure; any overdue deferred marker;
an executable vector without a requirement; an active requirement without one owner or declared evidence;
evidence with an unknown requirement; a self-asserted acceptance; and milestone closure while any
active requirement whose owner is an ancestor of or equal to the closing milestone lacks accepted
evidence. Thus every closure rechecks earlier owners rather than only requirements owned by that exact
milestone. M-R repeats closure over every requirement derived for the release profile.

Each consumer scenario records source/canonical raw, generated JavaScript before minification, shipped
minified bytes, gzip-9, Brotli-q11, Brotli-q5, parse time, retained memory, module/request count, and the
included graph. Brotli-q11 is a lab comparison; q5 is a delivery proxy. The chosen production host's

Each checked scenario manifest names its applicable `profileIds`, one owner milestone, an immutable
freeze deadline, the pack/build recipe and artifact-identity rule, import specifier, fixed fixture
hashes, raw-versus-parsed input, harness source and command hashes, runtime/browser/tool versions,
exact hardware or provisioned-host identity, cold/warm cache state, warm-up count, measured sample
count, concurrency, aggregation statistic and percentile, timeout and failed-sample treatment, proxy
inventory and estimation method, thresholds, and regression tolerances.
Network scenarios also lock origin/CDN and host profile, headers, cache/preload state, and measurement
region. Each immutable run attestation records the actual tarball, output-graph, data-derivative, and result hashes;
a new implementation digest identifies a new run without redefining the scenario. Changing the frozen
recipe, fixture, environment, method, or threshold creates a reviewed scenario revision and cannot be
compared as the same scenario.

M0 freezes every selected-profile scenario whose deadline is M0 and registers the owner/deadline for
the rest. A later scenario must freeze before its owner's implementation/evidence can count. The
selected profile mechanically defines which registered scenarios are applicable; deferred-profile
scenarios are catalog entries, not first-release gates.

Before plan approval fixes the M0 effort cap, the named production implementer, human reviewer, and
human decision owner run a dry calibration over all of `2.2`. In a scratch copy they classify every
checked block, split every normative clause, and draft one provisional `CAL-*` record per atomic
proposition using the candidate production marker/registry grammar. They also assign the proposed
`registrationBefore` frontier, owner, parity class,
evidence kind, and source anchor. Calibration IDs never enter `requirements.json` and acquire no
immutability. The reviewed bootstrap process mints M0-frontier production records; M0 mints the
remaining initial-slice records.

The append-only calibration artifact records the exact plan/schema/tool hashes; implementer, reviewer,
and decision owner; monotonic start/stop boundaries; accepted, split, merged, rejected, and reworked
record counts; separate agent authoring/review/rework wall minutes; separate active human implementer,
reviewer, and decision-owner minutes; and the accepted annotated-section and scratch-registry hashes.
Agent minutes per accepted record remain a throughput measure. The formal human-attention rate is
`(human implementer + human reviewer + human decision-owner minutes) / accepted records`; any
decision-owner work measured per batch rather than per record is added as a separate fixed allowance.
The initial-slice human registry allowance is that rate multiplied by the checked-inventory-derived

and separately estimated human schema/linter/tooling effort. Agent throughput receives a separate
planning allowance and is never substituted for the human-attention cap. The M0 combined-human-effort
cap must include the human allowance and all other M0 work. A change to the named people,
marker/schema workflow, or tooling that invalidates either measured rate requires a rerun or an
approved more-conservative rate.

initial registration slice, its source anchor, reduced `registrationBefore` frontier, and reviewed
anticipated atomic-record count. The allowance uses the sum of those reviewed counts; it may not
extrapolate from section word count alone. The calibration and inventory are preapproval inputs, while

clock begins
at approval, not at its eventual exit. M0 exit confirms the M2 duration/effort envelope or records an
explicit rebaseline, then computes the absolute M2 deadline as `M0ExitedAt + confirmedDuration`. The M2
clock and envelope begin at M0 exit and cover the complete M1 + M3a + M2 critical path: all engineering
and review effort charged to those milestones counts against it, including parallel work.

At the earlier of 50% elapsed time or 50% cumulative effort for either gate, the decision owner records
a checkpoint. M0's checkpoint must attach hashes for the corrected direct-locale contract, an
executable registry linter over the currently marked plan, and reproducible results for the required
lossless candidates. The M2 checkpoint must attach a running 0a root/core result in Node and one
exact-floor browser plus current M1/M3a evidence closure. If an artifact is absent or the named reviewer
does not approve the checkpoint, CI records the pause and cannot advance until an append-only outcome
approved by both decision owner and reviewer names exactly one of: stop; a release-profile/requirement
claim-cut migration; an in-cap
remediation plan with remaining work, owner, deadline, and reviewer approval; or a new cumulative
envelope with identified additional capacity. An unconstrained "continue" memo cannot resume work.

At 100% of either date or effort cap, an incomplete gate stops advancement. Continuing requires an
explicit new envelope plus either named scope/claim cuts or funded additional capacity; silently moving
the date or continuing an open-ended milestone is not permitted.

The checked capacity record is versioned and append-only. It names the approval commit/date, start
event, counted milestones/work categories, weekly commitments, ledger source, date/effort caps,
threshold calculations, checkpoint artifact hashes, approver, and every pause or rebaseline. Elapsed
time may toll only for a recorded external block approved by both decision owner and reviewer; effort
never tolls. A rebaseline preserves prior usage and history rather than resetting either counter. CI
and milestone review reject a missing, overdue, unapproved, or over-cap record.
